transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-06-28 08:37 UTC
Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees (calendar): Priya Desai (Redwood AE), Marco Alvarez (Redwood SE), Tina Rao (Redwood CSM); Dr. Lena Park (Kallisto Head of AI), Omar Reed (Platform Lead), Simone Patel (Procurement)

Summary:
Quick renewal-check and scope for extension: Kallisto is looking at a 12-month contract extension with a 2x capacity uplift and activation of an EU private region (VPC) for residency. Primary drivers: reduce p50/p95 latency in EU traffic, predictable unit economics during Q3 ramp, and SOC2 + KMS compliance for clinical PII. Agreed next steps: updated pricing, security docs, and a short private pilot for latency benchmarks.

Topics covered (auto): capacity uplift, EU region onramp, VPC/KMS, latency SLOs, pricing mechanics (reserved vs burst), rollout timeline, procurement windows.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Priya: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i'll kick us off. um, quick agenda — renewal timing, capacity ask, eu region onboarding questions and any blockers from procurement or security. 
[00:18] Dr. Lena: hi yeah thanks, morning, this should be, uh, fairly quick. essentially we're ready to extend for a year but we need two things — consistent latency for EU users and clear residency for patient data.
[00:31] Priya: totally, that's what we expected. marco from the se side is here to go over latency options and private deployment patterns. marco, take it away?
[00:40] Marco: thanks. so quick intro — we did a small internal bench a month ago with redwood dedi and saw the p50 at about 60ms for 8k context, p95 closer to 220ms depending on batch. those were in us-west. for eu we can route to eu geocluster; if you want private vpc/onprem like you mentioned, we do a private control plane + customer VPC with dedicated nodes. some customers call it Redwood Dedi or Redwood Private — transcription might flip names.
[01:10] Omar: quick clarifying q — when you say dedicated nodes, what's the guarantee vs shared hosted? like CPU/GPU contention at peak?
[01:20] Marco: good q. with dedicated pools you get reserved GPU capacity — we commit N cards for your slice. autoscaling policies are configurable but bursts above reserved capacity go to burst pool which is billed differently. contention is minimal on the reserved slice; the fallen-back burst path is shared. so if you need strict latency at peak you either size reserved capacity to cover peak or accept occasional fallbacks.
[01:45] Dr. Lena: we can't accept fallbacks that add 150ms regularly — we have clinical flows where under-200ms matters. our SLO target is p50 < 70ms, p95 < 220ms in eu.
[01:58] Marco: understood. rough approach — for p50 target set a reserved pool sized to handle 85-90% of baseline qps, then use small burst for rare spikes. also enable prefix/K-V cache for stable conversational prefixes, that shaves tokens and reduced latency.
[02:19] Simone: (procurement) just to scope cost, is reserved capacity a term contract? how flexible is it mid-year?
[02:26] Priya: yes reserved is contract-backed (monthly/annual commits). we can do step-up amendments mid-term but pricing changes depend on term. i can include a 2-step ramp schedule in the quote — e.g., start with 1.5x reserved for Q3, full 2x on Oct 1.
[02:44] Omar: for the eu vpc, what's the network egress path? do requests go across our VPC peering back to redwood control plane? i'm worried about double egress charges and routing complexity.
[02:58] Marco: good point — in private VPC we place serving nodes in your region and VPC. control plane is separate but telemetry and metrics go to the control plane over an encrypted management channel. egress for inference stays local, so you shouldn't see cross-region inference egress. we'll put a diagram in the architecture doc.
[03:20] Dr. Lena: can you support our KMS? we use Azure Key Vault backed HSM, we can't export keys.
[03:26] Marco: yes, we integrate with customer-managed KMS; we have docs for Azure Key Vault and AWS KMS. small caveat: some tokenization keys need to be available to the runtime key material path but we can keep model artifact encryption and logs in your KMS. we'll detail this in the security pack.
[03:44] Simone: procurement timeline — if the PO goes in mid-july what's realistic for EU activation?
[03:51] Priya: with a PO mid-July we can schedule provisioning for early August, private region activation usually takes 2-3 weeks depending on capacity and network approvals.
[04:05] Omar: any compliance packets? SOC2 and audit logs are a must. we need to hand to our legal for review.
[04:11] Tina (CSM): i can package SOC 2 Type II artifact set, audit log samples and an export of the per-route trace sheet. we'll also include RBAC and SSO (SAML) integration notes.
[04:28] Dr. Lena: perfect. on the latency bench — we want to replicate production traffic. i'll share 7-day traffic and sequence length histograms but can we do a 48-hour private pilot where you run our payloads against a dedicated slice?
[04:42] Marco: yes that's standard — we recommend a two-day live bench with your payloads plus our synthetic spikes to confirm p50/p95. we'll run KV caching scenarios and quantized model paths.
[04:56] Priya: to be clear, pilot doesn't need a signed contract but we'll need an acceptably scoped MSA addendum and NDA.
[05:05] Simone: do you have sample MSA language for trial pilots?
[05:09] Priya: yes — i'll attach a short pilot addendum to the quote.
[05:14] Dr. Lena: pricing — we saw a cost delta vs GoliathAI for eu traffic. your price for reserved capacity + burst needs to be competitive; otherwise we'll consider an all-hosted high-commit model.
[05:26] Priya: understood. i'll send a revised quote with tiered commit options: 12-month reserved with 20% discount vs 24-month option with incremental discount and a separate burst add-on for EU.
[05:40] Omar: technical question — does the KV cache persist across model patches/rollouts? we rely on cached prefixes and can't cold-start often.
[05:49] Marco: KV cache persists in the serving layer; we maintain cache across compatible model variants but major architecture changes or quantization swaps might flush cache. we have migration strategies — warmup requests, pre-seeding, and safe rollbacks.
[06:06] Dr. Lena: we run two model families: a retrieval-augmented summarizer and a clinical NER. the NER is latency-sensitive, summarizer less so. can you route services differently?
[06:17] Marco: yes, you can route by model family or route. you can pin NER to the reserved slice and set the summarizer to go to lower-cost pooled instances. we can also set automatic fallback policies.
[06:29] Simone: any penalties if we over-run reserved during a quarter?
[06:33] Priya: overage is billed at the burst rate, we can include usage smoothing credits for the first quarter for runway.
[06:40] (Brief cross talk)
[06:46] Dr. Lena: ok next — timeline — if we aim to sign by July 20 (end of week 3) does that align with your provisioning plans?
[06:53] Priya: yes, sign July 20ish -> provisioning in early Aug -> pilot mid-August -> go-live late Aug/Sept for EU gradual rollout.
[07:05] Marco: for pilot we'll need sample keys, traffic, and a CIDR block for the dev VPC. Omar if you can share those we'll schedule.
[07:14] Omar: i can share CIDR and traffic file by Friday. also note our internal security team may ask for wire-level diagrams and port lists.
[07:23] Marco: we'll include a minimal port list, management plane IPs, and an allowlist for the control plane.
[07:32] Dr. Lena: one more — do you support model quantization profiles? cost is a driver and we'd like to see how 4-bit/8-bit affects latency vs quality.
[07:41] Marco: yes, Redwood Optimize team provides quantization recommendations. we'll run a quality vs latency sweep during the pilot and include recommended quant profiles. often 4-bit gives good cost savings with minor quality degradation for some models but we should validate on your eval set.
[07:59] Simone: legal question — data residency: does go-live mean data stays in EU and never leaves? we need contract language.
[08:06] Tina: yes, private region + VPC ensures inference data remains in-region. control-plane telemetry metadata might traverse, but we can minimize and sign residency clauses in the agreement; we'll include specific contractual language.
[08:22] Dr. Lena: okay i'm comfortable with that as long as KMS is customer-managed.
[08:27] Marco: confirmed.
[08:29] Priya: wrapping up — recap and next steps: i will send updated quote with two ramp options and pilot addendum; marco sends pilot plan and sample scripts; tina sends SOC2 + SSO/KMS docs; omar shares traffic samples and CIDR. procurement to confirm PO windows.
[08:45] Simone: yes we'll try to move fast. procurement target is PO by July 12 internal review, sign by July 20 if nothing blocks.
[08:53] Dr. Lena: can you also include a short runbook for rollback if the pilot shows regressions? we need a safety net for clinical flows.
[08:59] Marco: yes, rollback and canary playbook included.
[09:03] Priya: perfect. thanks all, we'll follow up in email with attachments.

End of call.

Notes on transcript quality: some product names and acronyms may be slightly off (Redwood Dedi vs Dedicated, K-V cache spelled different), and there was a little crosstalk.

References/Artifacts mentioned: updated quote (to be attached), pilot addendum (MSA sample), SOC2 Type II evidence pack, network architecture diagram, benchmark plan and scripts.
